extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 named entity data
extraction.description: Language-independent named entity recognition data sets for English and German, containing four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations and miscellaneous.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus. The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters news stories and Frankfurter Rundshau newspaper articles.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 1996 to December 1996 (English) and August 1992 to December 1992 (German)
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed. An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development (tuning parameters), and testing named-entity recognition systems.

name.evidence: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German

description.evidence: We describe the CoNLL-2003 shared task: language-independent named entity recognition. We give background information on the data sets (English and German)... We will concentrate on four types of named entities: persons, locations, organizations and names of miscellaneous entities

isLiveDataset.evidence: The CoNLL-2003 named entity data consists of eight files covering two languages: English and German1. For each of the languages there is a training file, a development file, a test file and a large file with unannotated data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus... The text for the German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: This corpus consists of Reuters news stories... extracted from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundshau.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: Reuters news stories between August 1996 and August 1997. For the training and development set, ten days’ worth of data were taken from the files representing the end of August 1996. For the test set, the texts were from December 1996... All three of the training, development and test sets were taken from articles written in one week at the end of August 1992. The raw data were taken from the months of September to December 1992.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: for all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data... The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data, was done by hand at the University of Antwerp. Mostly, MUC conventions were followed (Chinchor et al., 1999). An extra named entity category called MISC was added to denote all names which are not already in the other categories.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger (Daelemans et al., 2002). The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger (Schmid, 1995).

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The leaming methods were trained with the training data. The development data could be used for tuning the parameters of the leaming methods... tested on the test data.
